title: Understanding Terminal Velocity
text: Terminal velocity is the constant speed that a freely falling object eventually reaches when the resistance of the medium prevents further acceleration. It can be calculated using the formula: $$v=sqrt((2mg)/(C_{d}pA))$$, $$where$$ $$m$$ $$is$$ $$mass$$, $$g$$ $$is$$ $$acceleration$$ $$due$$ $$to$$ $$gravity$$, $$C_{d}$$ is the drag coefficient, $$p$$ is the density of the fluid, and A is the cross-sectional area.

title: Calculate Terminal Velocity
text: Calculate the terminal velocity using the formula: $$v=sqrt((2\cdot80\cdot9.81)/(0.70\cdot1.21\cdot0.140))$$.

title: Convert to Kilometers per Hour
text: To convert the velocity from meters per second to kilometers per hour, multiply by $$3.6$$.

title: Final Conversion
text: Convert the calculated velocity to kilometers per hour: $$56.5\times3.6$$.
